findings.title: Full provider generations and profile wrappers can exceed their own read budgets
findings.description: prepare checks only the compact public view, then serializes private model instructions and native catalogs without enforcing the 4 MiB settings read limit. Two individually valid provider catalogs can therefore create a generation that read/verify refuses; activation stops services before this late failure. Profiles.save independently adds metadata around a valid near-limit settings object and can persist an oversized profile, after which Profiles.records/public and provider/read reject the retained profile.
evidence: .work/v240/full1-provider-size-probe.log: each catalog request 896915 bytes, combined settings 5404816 bytes, public 4019 bytes; persisted generation 5404817 bytes then read_json rejects corrupt_state.

.work/v240/full1-profile-size-probe.log: settings 4194293 bytes; saved profile 4194364 bytes; Profiles.records rejects Unsafe provider profile. Both probes used task-owned TemporaryDirectory fixtures; no production configuration was read or written.
findings.recommendation: Enforce exact UTF-8 serialized byte budgets including newline and profile wrapper before creating a generation/profile or stopping services. Add aggregate multi-provider and near-boundary profile regression cases; preserve existing data and bounded reads.

findings.title: Existing toolchain cache prevents a pinned CLI upgrade from completing
findings.description: Builder.toolchain reuses the fixed toolchain directory whenever its contents match the stored manifest, without binding that manifest to current Node/pnpm/Codex versions or distribution hashes. No control-update or application-update path refreshes this cache. An existing 0.164 installation therefore reuses 0.164 while preparing the 0.169 candidate, and the explicit runtime probe rejects it only after dependency fetch/install/build. Repeated attempts cannot self-correct and consume retained candidate slots. The final probe prevents publishing the old CLI; this is an upgrade blocker rather than a claim of silent successful downgrade.
evidence: .work/v240/full1-toolchain-version-probe.log: current CLI 0.169.0; a self-consistent cached 0.164.0 marker is accepted and download call count is zero. The fixture substitutes only durability barriers and uses no executable or network call.
Whole deploy reference search found toolchain creation/reuse only in build.py; operator.update invokes control-update/config-layer/HTTPS refresh/update without selecting current-version tooling.
findings.recommendation: Bind toolchain selection to the reviewed version, architecture and distribution digests, prepare a new immutable versioned generation when pins change, and preserve the old cache for recovery. Verify selected versions before expensive candidate work and add upgrade/reuse/interrupted-publication tests.
